question.text: An individual takes 90 s to climb up a stationary 15 m escalator. If the individual remains motionless on the same escalator while it operates, they reach the top in 60 s.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Determine the duration needed for the individual to walk upwards while the escalator is running.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Does this calculated time rely on the length of the escalator?

conditions: time taken walking on stationary escalator = 90 s
time taken standing on moving escalator = 60 s
walking speed relative to escalator is constant
escalator moves at a constant speed

solution.approach: Find the walking speed and the escalator speed separately, in escalator lengths per second, then add them for the combined speed.

steps.text: Write the walking speed as the escalator length divided by the walking time, and the escalator speed as the length divided by the moving time.
Add the two speeds, since walking on the moving escalator combines both motions.
Divide the escalator length by the combined speed to get the time; notice that the length appears in both the numerator and the denominator.
steps.why_this_step: Since t = L ÷ (L/90 + L/60), the length L cancels, so the time does not depend on how long the escalator is.

final_answer.value: 36 s; no, the answer does not depend on the escalator length, since the length cancels out of the calculation.

common_mistakes.text: Averaging the two given times as (90 + 60)/2 gives 75 s, which is not how the walking and escalator speeds combine.
